title: How to Build a Web3 Product that Users Love
summary: Creating a web3 product is challenging, but even more so is attracting and onboarding users. Learn about empathetic design and how you can onboard the masses with it.
author: Nathaniel Thoreson
body:
Creating a web3 product is not easy. Climbing the unending barrier of knowledge is riddled with obstacles like learning solidity, writing smart contracts, tokenomics, and more. But that's only half the battle. The other half is attracting and onboarding users.

Your web3 product is useless without users. No matter how innovative or revolutionary your product is, if no one knows about it or understands how to use your product, it will fail. Plain and simple. If you want to grow, you need to delight your users - all of them, regardless of their technical know-how.

But how do you do that in the web3 space? How do you attract and retain users unfamiliar with blockchain technology or intimidated by its complexity? How do you make your product accessible and appealing to the masses?

The answer is simple: bury the blockchain in the background.

Think about the iPod. When Apple launched the iPod in 2001, it changed how people listened to music. Its hardware was like nothing the world had ever seen. It would lay the foundation for future consumer products that defined the fourth industrial revolution.

Apple could have boasted its technical capability. After all, they spent billions of dollars and got the brightest minds to work on the product. But Steve Jobs knew that people wouldn't care. Instead of mentioning specific data storage capabilities or file transfer methods, Apple clearly articulated its value in one sentence: "1000 songs in your pocket." iPod wasn't for the hardware nerd. iPod was for anyone. Apple reflected that ideal in its design and messaging, a product strategy I call "empathetic design."

Empathetic Design was Apple's key to success. It's the key to any innovation that becomes widely adopted. Here are four ways that you can start to implement empathetic design into your web3 product to delight and attract billions of future users.

‍

#01 Optimize your user experience and user interface

‍
Using web3 products is already complicated, even for the most advanced web3 users. Managing wallets, securing keys, opting into tokens, paying gas fees, transactions, and signing transactions are all responsibilities that users take on. Each responsibility is a barrier that prevents users from enjoying your product. Don't let a poor user interface get even more in the way!

UI/UX is about making your product simple, beautiful, and understandable. Your users should know exactly what to do and how to do it. Without optimizing your design and user experience, your users will show up and quickly leave, never to return.
